copy.en:
Why do chameleons really change color?

More often it's to show their mood or control their body heat, not just to hide!
copy.tl:
Bakit talaga nagbabago ng kulay ang hunyango?

Mas madalas para ipahayag ang kalooban nito o ayusin ang init ng katawan, hindi lang para magtago!
copy.bis:
Ngano gyud nga mag-usab og kolor ang chameleon?

Kasagaran aron ipakita ang gibati o pag-ayo sa init sa lawas, dili lang aron motago!

Which animal changes color better, chameleon or octopus?

Surprise — it's the octopus! Chameleons aren't the only color-changers; octopuses are actually faster and better at switching color and texture.
copy.tl:
Sino ang mas magaling magpalit ng kulay, chameleon o octopus?

Sagot: ang pugita! Hindi lang chameleon ang nagpapalit ng kulay — mas mabilis at mas magaling pa ang pugita sa pagbabago ng kulay at texture.
copy.bis:
Kinsa'y mas maayo mo-usab og kolor, chameleon o octopus?

Tubag: ang kugita! Dili lang chameleon ang mousab og kolor — mas paspas ug mas maayo pa ang kugita sa pag-usab og kolor ug texture.

What unit measures electric charge?

It's measured in coulombs (C), named after the scientist Charles-Augustin de Coulomb!
copy.tl:
Anong yunit ang sumusukat ng electric charge?

Sinusukat ito sa coulombs (C), na ipinangalan kay siyentipikong si Charles-Augustin de Coulomb!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga yunit ang nagsukod sa electric charge?

Gisukod kini sa coulombs (C), nga ginganlan sa siyentistang si Charles-Augustin de Coulomb!

copy.tl: Ang cheetah ang pinakamabilis na hayop sa lupa — kaya nitong tumakbo ng halos 100 hanggang 110 kilometro kada oras, pero sa maikling sandali lang dahil mabilis itong mapagod.

Did you know food and fuel hold a special kind of power?

That stored power is called chemical energy! It's the energy waiting inside your food and fuel.
copy.tl:
Alam mo bang may espesyal na kapangyarihan ang pagkain at gasolina?

Ang enerhiyang nakaimbak sa pagkain at gasolina ay tinatawag na chemical energy!
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang pagkaon ug gasolina adunay espesyal nga gahum?

Ang enerhiya nga gitipigan sa pagkaon ug gasolina gitawag og chemical energy!

copy.en:
Why do you usually get chickenpox only once?

Chickenpox comes from a virus that causes itchy blisters. Your body remembers it after and can fight it off next time.
copy.tl:
Bakit minsan lang tayo nagkakabulutong-tubig?

Ang bulutong-tubig ay dulot ng virus na nagdudulot ng makating butlig. Naaalala ito ng katawan mo pagkatapos at kaya nang labanan sa susunod.
copy.bis:
Ngano kausa ra ta makakuha og bulutong-tubig?

Ang bulutong-tubig gikan sa virus nga hinungdan sa makatol nga butlig. Mahinumdoman kini sa imong lawas human niadto ug makasukol na sa sunod.

Kapag bumababa ang chlorophyll sa nalalantang dahon, lumilitaw na ang dilaw at kahel na pigment na dati ay nakatago!

How do the colors move in paper chromatography?

In paper chromatography, water rises up the paper and carries the colors upward with it!

Paano gumagalaw ang mga kulay sa paper chromatography?

Sa paper chromatography, umaakyat ang tubig sa papel at dinadala nito ang mga kulay paitaas!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglihok sa mga kolor sa paper chromatography?

Sa paper chromatography, mosaka ang tubig sa papel ug dad-on niini ang mga kolor pataas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When water drips on paper and ink spreads outward with a color streak at the edge, that's real-life chromatography happening!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets

Have you seen chromatography without knowing it?

Yes! When water drips on paper and ink spreads outward with a color streak at the edge, that's real-life chromatography happening!
copy.tl:
Nakita mo na ba ang chromatography nang hindi mo namamalayan?

Oo! Kapag natuluan ng tubig ang papel at kumalat ang tinta na may bahid ng kulay sa gilid, iyon ay totoong chromatography!
copy.bis:
Nakita na ba nimo ang chromatography nga wala nimo namatikdi?

Oo! Kung matuluan og tubig ang papel ug mokatag ang tinta nga naay bahid sa kolor sa kilid, kana tinuod nga chromatography!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets

copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, subukan ang chromatography gamit ang dahon! Durogin ito para hiwalayin ang kulay, at makikita mo ang nakatagong dilaw at orange, hindi lang berde.
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, sulayi ang chromatography gamit ang dahon! Dugmoka aron bulagon ang kolor, ug makita nimo ang tinagong dalag ug orange, dili lang berde.

Nganong nagkabulag ug nagkalain ang gilay-on sa pagsaka sa mga kolor?

Ang mga kolor nga sayon matunaw sa tubig mosaka og mas layo, mao nga magkabulag sila!

copy.tl: Ang breadboard ay plastic board na may butas para isingit ang electronic components at jumper wires nang walang solder. Ginagamit ito ng mga estudyante para i-test ang circuits!
copy.bis: Ang breadboard usa ka plastic board nga adunay mga butas para isingit ang electronic components ug jumper wires nga walay solder. Gigamit kini sa mga estudyante para i-test ang circuits!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When part of a circuit is broken or open, electricity cannot flow through it, so the bulb will not light up at all!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the effect of an open circuit but does not teach assembling or drawing a simple circuit, which is the explicit action of the competency. It is related background about circuit behavior, not direct support for the required skill.

copy.en: When part of a circuit is broken or open, electricity cannot flow through it, so the bulb will not light up at all!
copy.tl: Kapag may putol o bukas na bahagi sa isang circuito, hindi makakadaloy ang kuryente kaya hindi magliliwanag ang bombilya!
copy.bis: Kung adunay nabugto o bukas nga bahin sa circuito, dili makaagi ang kuryente busa dili mosiga ang bombilya!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Factories and big buildings in the Philippines use three-phase electricity — it delivers more power efficiently and gives steadier voltage for heavy motors.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that factories use three-phase electricity for efficiency and steady voltage. It does not describe how high voltage electricity is generated, safely distributed, or the roles of substations and electric meters, which are the core actions of G10-F-9.

copy.en: Factories and big buildings in the Philippines use three-phase electricity — it delivers more power efficiently and gives steadier voltage for heavy motors.
copy.tl: Ang mga pabrika at malalaking gusali sa Pilipinas ay gumagamit ng three-phase electricity — mas maraming kapangyarihan ang ibinibigay nito nang mahusay at mas matatag na voltage para sa malalaking motor.
copy.bis: Ang mga pabrika ug dagkong building sa Pilipinas naggamit ug three-phase electricity — mas daghang kapangyarihan ang ihatag niini nga mas maayo ug mas stable nga voltage para sa mga dagkong motor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Calamansi, dalandan, pomelo, and lemon all belong to the citrus family because they share sour, fragrant-skinned fruit!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions grouping fruits by a shared characteristic (citrus family), which is tangentially related to classification, but it does not use a table, does not classify into the named groups (flowering/non-flowering plants, animal groups, microorganisms), and does not teach the classification system required by the competency.

copy.en: Calamansi, dalandan, pomelo, and lemon all belong to the citrus family because they share sour, fragrant-skinned fruit!
copy.tl: Ang kalamansi, dalandan, suha, at lemon ay magkakapamilya na tinatawag na citrus dahil pare-parehong maasim at mabango ang balat!
copy.bis: Ang kalamansi, dalandan, suha, ug lemon managsoon nga gitawag og citrus kay tanan maaslom ug humot ang panit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's better for civets to gather coffee cherries freely in the wild than to be kept in cages, which can hurt their health.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses animal welfare (caging vs. wild) but does not directly teach the need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive. It implies a preference for wild conditions but lacks explicit conservation or environmental protection content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's better for civets to gather coffee cherries freely in the wild than to be kept in cages, which can hurt their health.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a human activity (caging civets) and its effect on an animal, but it does not describe effects on living things in an ecosystem, nor does it use secondary sources. It is a welfare statement, not an ecosystem-level impact description.

copy.en: It's better for civets to gather coffee cherries freely in the wild than to be kept in cages, which can hurt their health.
copy.tl: Mas mabuti para sa musang na mangalap ng kape nang malaya sa kalikasan kaysa ikulong sa hawla, dahil nakakasama ito sa kanilang kalusugan.
copy.bis: Mas maayo alang sa musang nga manguha og kape nga gawasnon sa kinaiyahan kaysa ibutang sa hawla, kay makadaot kini sa ilang panglawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The civet just passes coffee beans out in its poop after eating them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions beans passing through the civet and being eliminated in feces, but it does not trace food through the digestive tract, explain digestive processes, or use a labeled diagram as required. It is a misconception about coffee production, not instruction on the digestive system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The civet just passes coffee beans out in its poop after eating them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on digestion only indirectly by mentioning beans passing through the civet, but it does not describe how any human body system works, including the digestive system. It is a trivia card about civet coffee, not a description of body systems.

copy.en:
Does the civet really make kape alamid?

Not quite! The civet just passes coffee beans out in its poop after eating them. People collect those beans, clean them thoroughly, and roast them to make the coffee.
copy.tl:
Musang ba talaga ang gumagawa ng kape alamid?

Hindi talaga! Inilalabas lang ng musang ang butil ng kape sa dumi nito matapos kainin. Kinokolekta ito ng mga tao, nililinis nang husto, at iniihaw para maging kape.
copy.bis:
Ang musang ba gyud ang naghimo sa kape alamid?

Dili gyud! Igawas lang sa musang ang liso sa kape sa iyang tae human kan-a. Kolektahon kini sa mga tawo, limpyohan pag-ayo, ug sugbahon aron mahimong kape.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A civet makes a special scent from its body to mark its territory
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: to mark its territory and 'talk' to other civets
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not grow, respond, and reproduce as characteristics of living things.

copy.en: A civet makes a special scent from its body to mark its territory and 'talk' to other civets — almost like leaving them a message.
copy.tl: Ang musang ay gumagawa ng espesyal na amoy mula sa katawan nito para markahan ang teritoryo nito at makipag-usap sa ibang musang, parang nag-iiwan ito ng mensahe.
copy.bis: Ang musang mohimo og espesyal nga baho gikan sa lawas niini aron markahan ang teritoryo niini ug makigkomunikar sa ubang musang, morag nagbilin kini og mensahe.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists group living things into similar kinds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a general rationale for classification (grouping similar kinds for easier study). It does not use a table, does not name any of the required groups (flowering/non-flowering plants, mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians, fungi, bacteria), and does not teach how to classify living things into those groups. This is background motivation, not direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Scientists group living things into similar kinds — it makes the huge variety of life on Earth much easier to study.
copy.tl: Inuuri ng mga siyentipiko ang mga buhay na bagay sa magkakahawig na grupo, para mas madaling pag-aralan ang napakaraming uri nito.
copy.bis: Gigrupo sa mga siyentista ang mga buhing butang sa managsamang matang, aron sayon ra tun-an ang kadaghan sa mga matang niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Climate change adaptation means adjusting our lifestyle and activities to the changing climate and preparing for the future.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines climate change adaptation as adjusting lifestyle and preparing for the future. It does not address protecting or conserving the environment for living things to survive, which is the core of G3-L-8. The topic is related to the environment but does not directly support the conservation competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Climate change adaptation means adjusting our lifestyle and activities to the changing climate and preparing for the future.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan to conduct a survey to explore the possibilities for minimizing the negative impacts of human activities on an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a general definition of climate change adaptation. It does not involve planning a survey, exploring possibilities, or minimizing negative impacts of human activities on an ecosystem. The content is only broadly related to environmental issues and does not directly support the survey-planning competency.

copy.en:
How can people live safely as the climate changes?

By adapting! Climate change adaptation means adjusting our lifestyle and activities to the changing climate and preparing for the future.
copy.tl:
Paano makakapamuhay nang ligtas ang mga tao habang nagbabago ang klima?

Sa pamamagitan ng pag-aangkop! Ang climate change adaptation ay ang pagsasaayos ng ating pamumuhay at mga gawain sa nagbabagong klima at paghahanda para sa hinaharap.
copy.bis:
Unsaon sa mga tawo nga magpabiling luwas samtang nag-usab ang klima?

Pinaagi sa pagpahaom! Ang climate change adaptation mao ang pag-adjust sa atong pamaagi sa pagkinabuhi ug mga kalihokan sa nag-usab nga klima ug pagpangandam alang sa umaabot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Weather is how the atmosphere feels on a single day, while climate is the average weather pattern of a place over many years or decades.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines weather and contrasts it with climate, but does not identify any of the specific weather characteristics listed in the competency (air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, cloud cover). It provides only a general definition, not direct instructional support for identifying weather characteristics.

copy.en: Weather is how the atmosphere feels on a single day, while climate is the average weather pattern of a place over many years or decades.
copy.tl: Ang panahon (weather) ay ang kalagayan ng atmospera sa isang araw, samantalang ang klima ay ang karaniwang pattern ng panahon sa isang lugar sa loob ng maraming taon o dekada.
copy.bis: Ang panahon (weather) mao ang kahimtang sa atmospera sa usa ka adlaw, samtang ang klima mao ang kasagaran nga sumbanan sa panahon sa usa ka dapit sulod sa daghang tuig o dekada.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Climbing plants like rattan lean on other trees for support so they can reach sunlight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a climbing growth habit for reaching sunlight, but does not describe any specialized plant structure such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots. It does not directly support the competency's focus on specialized structures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so they can reach sunlight without growing their own thick, strong trunk
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a plant strategy to reach sunlight, which is an adaptation, but the competency specifically addresses adaptation to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods. Reaching sunlight is not an unfavorable condition of that type, and the card does not explain adaptation to drought or flooding.

copy.en: Climbing plants like rattan lean on other trees for support so they can reach sunlight without growing their own thick, strong trunk.
copy.tl: Ang mga umaakyat na halaman tulad ng uway ay gumagamit ng ibang puno bilang sandalan para maabot ang liwanag ng araw nang hindi kailangang magtayo ng sariling matibay na puno.
copy.bis: Ang mga mosaka nga tanom sama sa uway mogamit sa ubang kahoy isip sandiganan aron maabot ang kahayag sa adlaw nga dili kinahanglan magtukod og kaugalingong lig-on nga punoan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A clogged drain is like a closed door—water piles up and overflows onto the street.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a clogged drain as a local problem (water overflowing), but it does not identify how the issue could be addressed by science or mention waste treatment. It only gives a simple analogy about water flow, so it does not directly support the competency's action of identifying issues and how science can address them.

copy.en:
Clear drain vs. clogged drain—what's the difference?

A clear drain is like an open door—water flows out fast! A clogged drain is like a closed door—water piles up and overflows onto the street.
copy.tl:
Malinis vs. baradong kanal—ano ang pagkakaiba?

Ang malinis na kanal ay parang bukas na pinto—mabilis dumaloy ang tubig! Ang baradong kanal ay parang saradong pinto—naiipon at umaapaw sa kalsada.
copy.bis:
Limpyo vs. mababagan nga kanal—unsay kalainan?

Ang limpyo nga kanal sama sa abli nga pultahan—paspas modagayday ang tubig! Ang mababagan sama sa sirado nga pultahan—matapok ug moawas sa dalan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: misty, cloud-covered mountain forests where it makes its home
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that the cloud rat lives in misty mountain forests. It does not use a drawing or diagram, nor does it classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat into terrestrial, aquatic, or aerial groups. The habitat mention is related vocabulary but does not directly support the classification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: misty, cloud-covered mountain forests where it makes its home
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card names a habitat (mountain forests) but provides no list or table of animals and plants in that habitat. It does not support the skill of making a list or table with examples.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: misty, cloud-covered mountain forests where it makes its home
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the environment where the cloud rat lives but does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It is only a naming explanation, not an interdependence lesson.

copy.en:
Why is the cloud rat named that?

The cloud rat gets its name from the misty, cloud-covered mountain forests where it makes its home.
copy.tl:
Bakit tinawag itong cloud rat?

Pinangalanan ang cloud rat dahil sa maulap at maambong kagubatan sa bundok kung saan ito nakatira.
copy.bis:
Nganong ginganlan kining cloud rat?

Ginganlan ang cloud rat tungod sa maulap ug maambong kagubatan sa kabukiran diin kini nagpuyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cloud rats live up in trees and are active mostly at night
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a Philippine animal's habitat (trees) but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify it as terrestrial, aquatic, or aerial as required by the competency. It provides only a factual statement about cloud rats, not the required classification activity.

copy.en: Cloud rats live up in trees and are active mostly at night, so people rarely ever see them.
copy.tl: Ang cloud rat ay nabubuhay sa mga puno at gising lamang sa gabi, kaya bihira itong makita ng tao.
copy.bis: Ang cloud rat nagapuyo sa mga kahoy ug aktibo lamang sa gabii, mao nga panalagsa ra kini makita sa tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It forms when water vapor rises, cools, and turns into droplets.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes condensation (water vapor to droplets) but does not use diagrams or flowcharts as required by the competency, and it does not cover the other changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It forms when water vapor rises, cools, and turns into droplets.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water vapor turning into droplets, a part of the water cycle, but does not explain the role of the water cycle in the environment. It only gives a micro-level description of cloud formation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A cloud is made of millions of tiny water droplets or ice crystals floating in the air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water droplets and ice crystals (liquid and solid states) but does not identify the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) as a general concept. It does not teach that matter exists in three states.

copy.en: A cloud is made of millions of tiny water droplets or ice crystals floating in the air! It forms when water vapor rises, cools, and turns into droplets.
copy.tl: Ang ulap ay gawa sa milyon-milyong napakaliliit na patak ng tubig o kristal ng yelo na lumulutang! Nabubuo ito kapag ang singaw tumataas, lumalamig, at nagiging maliliit na patak.
copy.bis: Ang panganod hinimo sa minilyon ka gagmay nga tulo sa tubig o kristal sa yelo nga naglutaw! Maporma kini kung ang alisngaw mosaka, mobugnaw, ug mahimong gagmay nga tulo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the biggest fish is always female. If she dies, the largest male changes into a female
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sex change in clownfish, not the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not directly support teaching those characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the largest male changes into a female — a remarkable ability rare among animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of an animal changing sex, but not an example of adaptation to the environment like mimicry or camouflage. It does not directly support the competency's focus on environmental adaptation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the largest male changes into a female
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of: a) number of parents involved, and b) similarities of offspring to parents
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a sex change but does not differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of number of parents or offspring similarity. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Can a fish change from male to female?

In a group of clownfish, the biggest fish is always female. If she dies, the largest male changes into a female — a remarkable ability rare among animals.
copy.tl:
May isdang nagbabago ba mula lalaki tungo babae?

Sa grupo ng clownfish, ang pinakamalaki ay laging babae. Kapag namatay siya, ang pinakamalaking lalaki ay nagbabago at nagiging babae — kakaibang kakayahang bihira sa mga hayop.
copy.bis:
Naay isda ba nga mausab gikan sa laki ngadto babaye?

Sa grupo sa clownfish, ang pinakadako kanunay baye. Kon mamatay siya, ang pinakadako nga laki mausab ug mahimong baye — talagsaon nga abilidad nga panagsa ra sa mga hayop.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They share special stinging cells on their tentacles that catch and paralyze their food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: Tentacles catching food are not head, legs or wings used to move and gather food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They're all cnidarians
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They share special stinging cells on their tentacles that catch and paralyze their food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Stinging tentacles are invertebrate traits, not the difference between animals with and without a backbone.

copy.en:
What do jellyfish, anemones, and hydras share?

They're all cnidarians! They share special stinging cells on their tentacles that catch and paralyze their food.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakapareho ng dikya, anemone, at hydra?

Silang lahat ay cnidarian! May espesyal na stinging cells sa kanilang galamay na humuhuli at nagpaparalisa ng pagkain.
copy.bis:
Unsay pagkasama sa dikya, anemone, ug hydra?

Managsama silang cnidarian! Adunay espesyal nga stinging cells sa ilang galamay nga modakop ug mopa-paralisa sa pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The cobra is a venomous snake
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that a cobra is venomous and its venom can harm the body. It does not describe any outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their roles in movement or food gathering, which is the focus of G3-L-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The cobra is a venomous snake
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a snake and venom, which could be loosely related to animal adaptations, but it does not describe how the animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it use secondary sources or give an example like mimicry or camouflage. It only states a fact about venom, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The cobra is a venomous snake — its venom can seriously harm the body.
copy.tl: Ang cobra ay isang makamandag na ahas na may lasong nakakasama sa katawan.
copy.bis: Ang cobra usa ka makahilo nga bitin nga ang iyang hilo makadaot sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cockroaches usually come out at night and hide during the day
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a nocturnal behavior of cockroaches but does not explain how animals have changed to better suit their environment, nor does it mention mimicry, camouflage, or any evolutionary adaptation. It is only tangentially related to animal behavior.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cockroaches usually come out at night and hide during the day
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe growth, response, or reproduction. Nocturnal activity is a behavior, not one of the three listed characteristics of living things. It shares the topic of living things but provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: Cockroaches usually come out at night and hide during the day, so we may not notice the germs they leave behind!
copy.tl: Karaniwang lumalabas ang ipis kapag gabi at nagtatago kung araw, kaya hindi natin agad nakikita ang dumi nilang naiiwan!
copy.bis: Kasagaran mogawas ang ipis kung gabii ug motago kung adlaw, mao nga dili dayon nato makita ang hugaw nga ilang mabilin!
